standard_prerequisites.name: The cone sequence of the identity
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Definition definition-cone and the admissible short exact sequence x to C(1_x) to x[1]
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the natural morphism x to C(1_x) fitting the admissible sequence, out of which the admissible monomorphism tilde-alpha is assembled.

core_obligations: The factorization object (proof lines 3949-3960): by axiom (A) take tilde-y = y direct-sum C(1_x) with splittings s, pi and t, p, so that 1 on tilde-y equals s pi plus t p; tilde-alpha : x to tilde-y is induced by alpha on y and the natural morphism x to C(1_x) from the admissible sequence.

Admissible monomorphism and exactness (proof lines 3962-3978): the degree-0 morphism beta : tilde-y to x induced by the cone map C(1_x) to x and the zero map y to x makes tilde-alpha fit the admissible short exact sequence x to tilde-y to x[1], so tilde-alpha is an admissible monomorphism with pi tilde-alpha = alpha and pi s = 1_y.

The homotopy (proof lines 3980-4016): writing 1_x as d(h) for a degree -1 map h, the difference 1 on tilde-y minus s pi equals t p, which equals t (d h) p by lemma-id-cone-null, and this is d(t h p) since d t = d p = 0; hence s pi is homotopic to the identity.
proof_roadmap: Form the direct sum with the cone of the identity and write its splitting identities.
Assemble tilde-alpha from alpha and the cone sequence and verify it is an admissible monomorphism with the required compositions.
Compute the homotopy 1 - s pi = t p = t (d h) p = d(t h p) through the null-cone lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma factors any morphism of the differential graded category through an admissible monomorphism that admits a retraction split up to homotopy (statement lines 3937-3953). The proof (lines 3955-4016) is a hands-on construction: the direct-sum object from axiom (A) with its splitting identities, the assembly of tilde-alpha from the cone sequence of the identity and the verification that it sits in an admissible short exact sequence, and the explicit three-line homotopy computation 1 - s pi = t p = t (d h) p = d(t h p) using the null-cone lemma. H2: short, but the splitting bookkeeping and the homotopy computation are the argument and the result underpins the cone-factorization technology of the chapter.
